sources.entry: Collective Access - Providence - Highly configurable Web-based framework for management, description, and discovery of digital and physical collections supporting a variety of metadata standards, data types, and media formats. (Source Code) GPL-3.0 PHP

summary.one_liner: Providence is the back-end cataloging application of CollectiveAccess, a configurable web-based system for managing, describing, and discovering digital and physical collections.
summary.what_it_does: Providence is the cataloging component of the CollectiveAccess suite, used for managing, describing, and discovering complex digital and physical collections in museum, archival, and research settings. According to the README, it is highly configurable and supports a variety of metadata standards, data types, and media formats, including documents, images, audio, video, and 3D. Version 2.0 adds features such as change tracking over time (for example location history and provenance), improved search indexing, background processing for media and indexing tasks, and BagIT export for digital preservation systems. It also lists a GraphQL-based API, a data replication system for synchronizing CollectiveAccess instances, and import formats including METS, MODS, and Dublin Core XML. Pawtucket2 is a separate companion application that publishes public-facing websites from Providence data.
use_cases: describe and search physical and digital objects
publish public collection websites with Pawtucket2
transcribe audio and video with Whisper
how_to_run: Ensure the server meets the requirements (README states PHP 8.2 or 8.3; 8.4 being tested)
Download the Providence 2.0 tar.gz or zip release and follow the installation instructions
For development branches: git clone the repository, then git checkout develop
Run composer.phar install from the repository root to install third-party libraries
Upgrading from 1.7.x: back up the database and configuration, replace files while preserving media and app/conf/local, then run caUtils update-from-1-7
Upgrading from 1.6 or older: update to 1.7 first, then follow the 1.7 instructions
notable: Supports imports including METS, MODS, Dublin Core XML, EHive, and iDigBio
Tracks changes such as location history and provenance over time
Optional automated translation of profile text via Google Translate or DeepL
Automated audio/video transcription via OpenAI Whisper
Companion front-end application Pawtucket2 for public-access websites
caveats: Versions before PHP 8.2 are unsupported; the README says it can be made to work on 7.4 but this is not supported
Upgrading from 1.7 may take several hours on large systems because the update regenerates sortable values and rebuilds the search index
Upgrading from 1.6 or older requires first upgrading to 1.7
